transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Anderson. I wanted to come by and talk to you about how things have gone since you arrived.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you coming in. Although, the nurse already gave me the gist of the situation while you were away.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, yeah. Well, I'm sorry for any confusion regarding the timing of your arrival and the triage process. We were really busy in the emergency department today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm less concerned about how busy you were and more concerned about why I was sitting in the waiting room for three hours when I had clear focal neurological deficits.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the system can be quite overwhelming during peak hours. There were a few issues with how the initial assessment was recorded.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Let's be precise. Were you categorized as low-acuity despite your symptoms?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some a bit of a disconnect in the communication flow during the intake process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is a very polished way of saying the triage was wrong. Because of that delay, I missed the window for the clot-busting medication, didn't I?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is frustrating. We are focusing now on the next steps for your recovery and making sure we monitor your stability.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It isn't frustrating, Doctor. It is a clinical failure. I spend my days managing hospital administration; I know exactly what a thrombolysis window is and I know that once it closes, the damage is permanent.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're upset, and I get that. But looking at the current imaging, we are doing everything we can now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not upset. I am asking for a factual account of why the protocol failed. Who made the decision to keep me in the waiting room?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, the way the triage flow works is—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not finished. I want to know if this is being logged as a sentinel event.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient in a moment, so I want to make sure we get through this quickly. The point is that we are moving forward now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're rushing me. I am the patient in this scenario. I want a clear explanation of the error and a copy of the triage notes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sure we can get those sorted. I'll see what I can do about the paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When exactly will I see those notes? And who is the attending physician overseeing the review of this delay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the morning progresses. Just stay tuned for an update or maybe an email from the department.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a timeline. I want a meeting with the Chief of Medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But as I said, we're just trying to keep things moving.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have yet to actually tell me what happened. You've used words like "disconnect" and "issues." Did the triage nurse miss the stroke screen or did the screen not trigger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were just some things that didn't go quite right with the initial processing of your charts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is completely unacceptable. You are avoiding the facts of the case.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't feel a certain way. I am observing a failure in transparency.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We're doing our best here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Your best resulted in a permanent deficit. I expect a written summary of the triage failure by tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll look into it. I really have to get going now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We are not done here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll stop by later. We'll figure something out.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('get through this quickly', 'have to get going now') and interrupts the patient.

E.justification: Resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes like 'disconnect in the communication flow' and 'things that didn't go quite right'.

A.justification: Responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system', 'the triage flow', and 'the intake process'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand this is frustrating', 'I can see you're upset') without specific engagement or naming emotions back.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague responses ('we'll see how the morning progresses', 'we'll figure something out') without timelines or concrete steps.
